notes: Each of the 12 LED blocks connects one Mega PWM pin (2-13, copy n -> pin n+1) through a 220 ohm resistor to an LED anode; cathodes go via a black jumper to the shared ground rail, which is wired to Mega GND.

Fix: every wire end now uses its own breadboard hole. The ground rail is one strip; the Mega GND wire uses tn.1 and the 12 cathode jumpers use tn.2 through tn.13 (copy n -> tn.n+1), so no hole is shared.
Exact breadboard columns are chosen for a clean layout (copy n uses column 2n-1 for resistor/anode and column 2n for cathode); the image spaces them irregularly but the connectivity is the same.
The breadboard is oriented per the catalogue: bank 't' rows a-e, bank 'b' rows f-j; resistors straddle the centre gap.
The Mega GND port is assumed to be named 'GND.1' (catalogue port list truncated).
The anode is the longer LED leg; in the image the LED leg next to the resistor column is the anode, the other is the cathode.
Resistor value 220 ohm per the manual.
